title: Create Compact Model Signals Library & Continuous Competitive Tracker
creator: Asha Mehra
description: Objective: build a lightweight, queryable signals library that captures high-frequency market signals for open and commercial LLMs and a continuous competitive tracker that surfaces meaningful drift and capability changes. Scope: (1) compact data model and schema for signals (latency benchmarks, token pricing, quantization support, availability events, release cadence, notable feature flags), (2) collection pipelines for automated scraping + curated manual inputs, (3) a minimal dashboard and alerting rules for PM/Eng to detect regressions and supply risks, (4) a public-facing summary deck template for GTM. Deliverables: signals schema document, ETL pipeline PoC ingesting three model sources, a hosted dashboard with 4 KPIs, and an alert rule set with runbook. Success metrics: baseline ingestion of 3 model families within 4 weeks, end-to-end pipeline SLA >= 95% run success, median time-to-detect high-impact change <= 3 business days, and PM satisfaction >= 80% in pilot. Constraints: must avoid heavy infra investment; prefer serverless or lightweight cron workers for first iteration. Privacy/compliance: do not store customer PII; classify all sources and maintain provenance metadata.
acceptance_criteria: Signals schema published in Confluence and approved by Research and Eng
Automated ingest pipeline (cron or event-driven) collects signals from 3 distinct public sources and one internal monitored feed
Dashboard shows model availability, median latency trend, price change events, and quantization adoption per model family
Two alerting rules implemented (availability drop, price/latency delta beyond threshold) with documented runbook
Pilot feedback from at least 3 PMs and 2 SREs captured and synthesized

notes: Trade-off: avoid building heavy normalization early; store raw payloads and apply normalization in downstream queries to speed iteration.
Decision: prioritize availability, price, latency, and quantization signals for MVP because they most directly map to customer-facing SLAs and procurement decisions.
Trade-off: forgo real-time streaming for MVP; acceptable polling cadence set to 12 hours to reduce engineering cost.
